target_paper_title: OpenWorldSAM: Extending SAM2 for Universal Image Segmentation with Language Prompts

gold_annotations.topic: This paper studies open-vocabulary image segmentation with language prompts. It aims to extend SAM2 from interactive visual prompting to a unified system that supports category-level semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation as well as sentence-level referring expression segmentation, while preserving efficiency and zero-shot generalization to unseen categories.
gold_annotations.golden_gap: The paper identifies two main limitations in prior work. First, earlier open-vocabulary segmentation methods often rely on two-stage proposal-and-classification pipelines or heavy generalist models, which either struggle with complex language queries, focus only on limited segmentation settings, or require resource-intensive pre-training. Second, existing SAM-based language extensions either depend on costly LLM-centric designs or remain constrained to single-object queries. The paper also argues that common global-matching evaluation used by prior methods creates label ambiguity on large-vocabulary datasets, unfairly penalizing semantically reasonable predictions.
gold_annotations.golden_method: The proposed method, OpenWorldSAM, extends SAM2 with a lightweight language adapter while freezing the heavy SAM2 and vision-language backbones. An image and text prompt are jointly encoded by BEiT-3, projected into SAM2's prompt space, then expanded into multiple prompt queries using learnable positional tie-breaker embeddings so one language prompt can segment multiple object instances. A 3-layer soft-prompting Transformer applies self-attention and cross-attention between these language-aware queries and SAM2 image features, after which SAM2's mask decoder predicts masks conditioned directly on the text prompt. Training uses Hungarian matching and focal loss, and only the projector, tie-breakers, and soft-prompting layers are learned.
gold_annotations.gold_experiment: The paper trains on COCO2017-Stuff with panoptic annotations and evaluates zero-shot transfer on eight segmentation tasks across ADE20K-150/857, PASCAL VOC-20, PASCAL Context-59/459, ScanNet-20/40, and SUN-RGBD-37 using PQ, mAP, and mIoU. It also fine-tunes on RefCOCOg UMD and reports cIoU for referring expression segmentation. The experiments compare against open-vocabulary and unified segmentation baselines such as X-Decoder, APE, OVSeg, MaskCLIP, and OpenSeeD, and against SAM-language models including EVF-SAM, LISA, GLaMM, and u-LLaVA for referring segmentation. Reported results include state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on most evaluated segmentation benchmarks, 74.0 cIoU on RefCOCOg, analysis of oracle-prompt versus global-matching evaluation, and ablations on the multi-modal encoder, trainable modules, positional tie-breakers, number of tie-breaker tokens, and cross-attention depth.
